notes: Both configurations score 100% pass rate with zero variance - these assertions do not currently differentiate the skill from a no-skill baseline.

This is expected, not a red flag: every test run (with_skill and without_skill alike) was constrained by the test harness itself to stop the instant it reached the real Naver login wall, since no real account credentials exist for automated testing. That constraint - not the skill - is what both configurations are satisfying.

The baseline sessions independently guessed Naver Blog as the target platform and independently avoided entering credentials, purely from general safety norms and this project's Korean-language/CLAUDE.md context - so the current assertion set (Playwright MCP usage, correct platform, no credential entry, explicit handoff message, correctly not re-asking for already-given info) is really testing general model safety and reasonable judgment, not skill-specific value.

The skill's actual differentiators - which template to recommend from Naver's in-editor 템플릿 panel, whether the drafted body matches current Naver Blog reading/SEO conventions, whether the 저장 (temp-save) -> approval -> 발행 (publish) gate is respected, and correct handling of Naver's four-way 공개 설정 (전체공개/이웃공개/서로이웃공개/비공개) - all live on the far side of a real login and can't be exercised by an unauthenticated subagent.

Where the with_skill runs visibly do more than baseline: they cite the skill's specific section numbers and terminology (§2/§3/§7, 저장 vs 발행, the four granular 공개 설정 options) in their 'planned next steps' writeups, while baseline runs describe the same intent in vaguer terms and in eval 2's baseline case, offer the user an extra fallback path (write a plain-text draft now, publish manually later) that isn't part of the skill's flow. This is a qualitative signal, not something the current quantitative assertions capture - worth checking in the Outputs tab of the viewer.

Time delta (+6.9s favoring baseline) is not meaningful at n=1 per configuration and reflects incidental differences like a transient tool error the eval-0 baseline recovered from, not a real speed cost of the skill.

Recommendation for a future iteration: if there is ever a disposable/test Naver account available, re-run these evals with real login to actually exercise and grade the template-recommendation and draft-writing steps, which is where this skill is supposed to earn its value.
